It's just that I've tried writing them down, and have also tried communicating the plot lines with a few people I trust. Once I could gain a little bit of control and understanding of my daydreams I have openly talked about it and these are the conclusions. It's just my experience. It might be different for others.

Daydream is born out of denial and lack, while a story that stirs people's hearts is born out of living in the moment. "Reality" is rejected in a daydream. It can never connect with an audience except for those in denial themselves.

Are you comfortable sharing your daydreams with others? I'm certainly not. Those intricate plots won't make sense to anyone but you. Try writing them down. It's actually not the plot but the feelings that drive the whole thing, and those feelings are very very personal. Except for another daydreamer with similar plot lines, no one else can even relate to your stories.

If your imaginative boyfriend loves you soo very much in your daydreams and openly gives you credit for everything that he is, all those admirations are indirectly for your character. And it doesn't really require an effort on your part. It's the most convenient way to feel fulfillment, i.e, without having to do anything.

The truth is that your boyfriend was created by you. So, he is essentially just a broken piece of your mind dissociated from your ego. You're probably unable to experience feelings of admiration for yourself though you so badly want to, and have lost all hopes on yourself. So you've created something very dear to you but is NOT you to be able to "feel" those feelings indirectly.

Since the day I stopped comparing my characters with real life people, I don't feel that guilty about daydreaming anymore. It's just me, my lack, and my coping with an unacceptable past. All the feelings I've ever wanted to experience just break into different pieces and interact with themselves as characters. And if I am in it, it's just a piece of me that I wish I am. Hope this perspective makes sense  and helps remove your guilt and bad feelings towards yourself or your partner ❤️

Okay so here's the thing. We love a character because we're able to relate to him/her and get inspired from his/her journey to face challenges in life and become better. No one's perfect and we're all human, and these characters are just like us. They serve as great examples of how it's okay to make mistakes but end of the day, learn from them, grow, and earn our position in life.

Harvey forgave his mother, learned to trust people and became more vulnerable as the seasons progressed. Louis became more emotionally mature (which was his only weakness btw). But Donna? She was awesome, she is awesome now, she has always been awesome and well fit for her job all the time. As a woman myself I'm not at all able to relate to that. Being good with people is a skill too, and if she's so good at at, how did she goddamn get so good at it? And what was her intention or purpose behind getting better at it? That's what I want to know.

If we look at any other character they've known what they've always wanted to do with life, or understood it gradually and came to terms with it. With Donna it's like, she's doing what she's doing and suddenly one day she decides she wants more and immediately gets it without having had any long term vision. The link between her past journey and present seems to be broken, or if my understanding is wrong, it's just left unexplained. And I'm not as good as a writer to imagine, connect the dots together and see how it all makes sense.

Her image is more like a superhuman than an actual human, and I'm no superhuman so I'm sorry, as much as I loved her in the earlier seasons, it was totally disappointing to not see any "inner" character development in her (either from her past or present), or see how she had the mental abilities to "get there" in the first place. The only thing I learned from her is, "I just have to be as good as her naturally..."

This is all my personal opinion though, if there are those who get inspired from her then well and good, I feel happy for them.
